question.prompt: Pablo buys popsicles for his friends. The store sells single popsicles for \(\$1\) each, \(3\)-popsicle boxes for \(\$2,\) and \(5\)-popsicle boxes for \(\$3.\) What is the greatest number of popsicles that Pablo can buy with \(\$8?\)

solutions.title: Use the lowest unit price
solutions.explanation:
The lowest price per popsicle comes from a five-popsicle box:
\[
\frac35=0.60\text{ dollars per popsicle}.
\]
The other options cost \(1\) dollar and \(2/3\) dollar per popsicle, so every purchase costs at least \(0.60\) dollar per popsicle. Therefore, buying \(14\) would cost at least
\[
14(0.60)=8.40>8.
\]
Pablo can buy at most \(13\).

He can attain this bound with two five-popsicle boxes and one three-popsicle box. They cost \(2\cdot3+2=8\) dollars and contain \(2\cdot5+3=13\) popsicles.

The greatest number is \(\boxed{13}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
